headline: Dudhkumar river dyke collapse: 5,000 families stranded in Kurigram
summary: A 40-metre breach in the river protection embankment has inundated eight villages, worsening an already dire flood situation in the region.
details: A 40-metre section of the Dudhkumar river protection dyke collapsed in the Muriarhat area of Bamandanga union, Nageshwari, under the pressure of strong currents. This breach has allowed floodwaters to surge into nearby villages, leaving approximately 5,000 families stranded.

According to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), the Dudhkumar river was flowing 22 centimetres above its danger level at the Pateshwari point. The river has remained above the danger mark since yesterday morning.

The collapse has submerged eight villages in Bamandanga union, flooding homes, rural roads, and critical Aman seedbeds. Residents are now forced to travel by small boats or banana-stem rafts, with many surviving on dry food.

Across the Rangpur region, including Lalmonirhat, Kurigram, and Gaibandha, more than 20,000 families have been stranded over the past two days. Local administrations are currently distributing relief materials and dry food.

While the Teesta river's water level has fallen below the danger mark, the BWDB warns that the Dharla river is rising rapidly. If it crosses the danger level within 24 hours, fresh flooding could hit bankside areas.

The Water Development Board is working to reinforce the damaged dyke with bamboo piling and sand-filled geobags. Riverbank erosion has already been reported at 38 locations across Kurigram, washing away farmland and homesteads.

headline: Drug addict man threatens to kill son for ransom from wife in Gazipur
summary: A 40-year-old man allegedly held a knife to his 14-year-old son's throat and sent a threat video to his wife to demand money for drugs.
details: A complaint has been filed against Moksed Ali, 40, of Beldia village in Sreepur, Gazipur, for allegedly threatening to kill his own 14-year-old son.
The accused allegedly lured the boy, who resides at a madrasa, to a secluded location and recorded a video while holding a knife to the child's throat and chest.
Moksed then sent the footage to his wife, Yasmin Akter, demanding money to buy narcotics, as he has long been addicted to drugs.
The video, which circulated on social media, shows the child lying unconscious with a white cloth wrapped around his head while the father threatened his wife.
Following a complaint by Yasmin Akter, Sreepur Police rescued the child immediately and took him to a hospital for treatment.
Yasmin told police that her husband had frequently abused her to force her to obtain money for his drug addiction.
Sreepur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shahinur Alam confirmed that legal proceedings are underway and the accused will be brought to justice.
